chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and another, from Sahl, from Muhammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn altogether, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir and Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Abi al-Daylam, from Abu Abdillah (عليه السلام), who said:

Musa (عليه السلام) bequeathed to Yusha' ibn Nun, and Yusha' ibn Nun bequeathed to a descendant of Harun, and he did not bequeath to his own son nor to a descendant of Musa. Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, has the choice; He chooses whom He wills from among whom He wills.

And Musa and Yusha' gave glad tidings of the Messiah (عليه السلام). So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent the Messiah (عليه السلام), the Messiah said to them: There shall soon come after me a Prophet whose name is Ahmad, from the descendants of Isma'il (عليه السلام), who will come confirming me and confirming you, and my proof and your proof. And after him it continued among the disciples, among the entrusted preservers. Allah, the Exalted, only named them the preservers because they were entrusted with preserving the Greatest Name, and it is the Book by which the knowledge of everything is known, which was with the Prophets (صلوات الله عليهم).
Allah, the Exalted, says: “And We certainly sent messengers before you and sent down with them the Book and the Balance.”

The Book is the Greatest Name, and it is only recognized through what is called the Book: the Tawrah, the Injil, and the Furqan. Within it is the Book of Nuh, and within it is the Book of Salih, Shu'ayb, and Ibrahim (عليه السلام).
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed: “Indeed, this is surely in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa.”
So where are the scriptures of Ibrahim? The scriptures of Ibrahim are only the Greatest Name, and the scriptures of Musa are the Greatest Name.

The bequest continued in one scholar after another until they handed it over to Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله). So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), the descendants of the preservers submitted to him, while Banu Isra'il denied him. And he called to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and strove in His way.

Then Allah, Majestic is His remembrance, revealed to him: Proclaim the merit of your wasi. So he said: My Lord, the Arabs are a harsh people; there has not been among them a book, nor has a prophet been sent to them, and they do not know the merit of the prophet-hoods of the Prophets (عليهم السلام), nor their nobility, and they will not believe me if I inform them of the merit of my Ahl al-Bayt.
So Allah, Majestic is His remembrance, said: “And do not grieve over them, and say: Peace, for they shall soon know.”
So he mentioned something of the merit of his successor, and hypocrisy fell into their hearts. Thus the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) knew that and what they were saying.

So Allah, Majestic is His remembrance, said: “O Muhammad, We certainly know that your breast is constrained by what they say; for surely they do not call you a liar, but the wrongdoers reject the signs of Allah.”

But they denied without any proof for themselves. The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) used to conciliate them and seek the support of some of them against others, and he continued bringing forth for them something concerning the merit of his successor until this surah was revealed. Then he argued against them when he was informed of his death and his soul was announced to him.
So Allah, Majestic is His remembrance, said: “So when you are free, then appoint; and to your Lord turn with longing.”
Meaning: when you are free, then raise your standard and proclaim your successor, and make his merit publicly known to them.

So he (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: Whomever I am his mawla, then Ali is his mawla. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, and be the enemy of whoever is his enemy—three times. Then he said: I shall certainly send a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger love him; he is not one who flees—thereby alluding to the one who returned, calling his companions cowardly and them calling him cowardly.

And he (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: Ali is the chief of the believers. And he said: Ali is the pillar of the religion. And he said: This is the one who will strike the people with the sword upon the truth after me. And he said: The truth is with Ali wherever he inclines. And he said: I am leaving among you two matters; if you hold fast to them, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the people of my house, my progeny. O people, listen, and I have conveyed. You shall come to me at the Pond, and I shall ask you about what you did concerning the two weighty things; and the two weighty things are the Book of Allah, Majestic is His remembrance, and my Ahl al-Bayt. So do not precede them lest you perish, and do not teach them, for they are more knowledgeable than you.

So he continued to present the merit of his Ahl al-Bayt in speech and clarify it to them through the Qur'an: “Allah only desires to remove impurity from you, O Ahl al-Bayt, and to purify you thoroughly.” And He, Mighty is His remembrance, said: “And know that whatever you gain as spoils, then indeed for Allah is one-fifth of it, and for the Messenger, and for the near relatives.” Then He said: “And give the near relative his due.”
So it was Ali (عليه السلام), and his right was the bequest that was made for him, and the Greatest Name, and the inheritance of knowledge, and the transmitted traces of the knowledge of prophethood.
So He said: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for the near kin.” Then He said: “And when the buried one is asked, for what sin she was killed.”
Meaning: I ask you concerning the love whose merit I sent down upon you—the love of the near kin—for what sin did you kill them?
And He, Majestic is His remembrance, said: “So ask the أهل الذكر if you do not know.”

He said: The Book is the Reminder, and its people are the family of Muhammad (عليه السلام). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded that they be asked, and the people were not commanded to ask the ignorant.

And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, called the Qur'an a Reminder, so Blessed and Exalted is He said: “And We sent down to you the Reminder so that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them, and that perhaps they may reflect.” And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: “And indeed it is surely a reminder for you and for your people, and you shall soon be questioned.”

And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: “Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority among you.” And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: “And if they had referred it to Allah and to the Messenger and to those vested with authority among them, those among them who derive it would have known it.”
Thus He referred the matter—the affair of the people—to those vested with authority among them, those whose obedience He commanded and to whom He commanded matters be referred.

So when the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) returned from the Farewell Hajj, Jibra'il (عليه السلام) descended upon him and said: “O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord; and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.”

So he called the people and they gathered, and he ordered concerning some trees, and their thorns were swept away. Then he (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: O people, who is your guardian and has more authority over you than your own selves? They said: Allah and His Messenger. So he said: Whomever I am his mawla, then Ali is his mawla. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him and be the enemy of whoever is his enemy—three times.

Then the thorn of hypocrisy fell into the hearts of the people, and they said: Allah, Majestic is His remembrance, never sent this down upon Muhammad at all; he only intends to elevate the arm of his cousin.

Then when he came to al-Madinah, the Ansar came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah, Majestic is His remembrance, has been good to us and honored us through you and through your settling among us. Allah has gladdened our friend and cast down our enemy. Delegations may come to you while you do not find what to give them, and then the enemy would gloat over you. So we would like that you take a third of our wealth, so that when a delegation from Makkah comes to you, you would find what to give them.

But the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) did not answer them with anything, and he was waiting for what would come to him from his Lord. Then Jibra'il (عليه السلام) descended and said: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for the near kin.”

And he did not accept their wealth. So the hypocrites said: Allah did not send this down upon Muhammad; he only intends to elevate the arm of his cousin and impose his Ahl al-Bayt upon us. Yesterday he said: Whomever I am his mawla, then Ali is his mawla; and today: Say, I do not ask of you any reward except love for the near kin. Then the verse of khums was sent down to him, and they said: He intends to give them our wealth and our spoils.

Then Jibra'il came to him and said: O Muhammad, you have fulfilled your prophethood and completed your days, so place the Greatest Name, the inheritance of knowledge, and the traces of the knowledge of prophethood with Ali (عليه السلام). For I have never left the earth without there being in it a scholar by whom My obedience is known, by whom My wilayah is known, and who is a proof for those born between the passing of one Prophet and the emergence of the next Prophet. He said: So he bequeathed to him the Greatest Name, the inheritance of knowledge, and the traces of the knowledge of prophethood; and he bequeathed to him a thousand words and a thousand gates, each word and each gate opening a thousand words and a thousand gates.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: the Prophet’s household, presented here as purified and authoritative
key_terms.أُولِي الْأَمْرِ: those vested with authority whose obedience and reference are commanded
key_terms.الثَّقَلَيْنِ: the two weighty trusts: the Book of Allah and the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.الِاسْمُ الْأَكْبَرُ: the Greatest Name, a supreme divine trust associated with total sacred knowledge
key_terms.الْمَوَدَّةَ فِي الْقُرْبَىٰ: love for the Prophet’s near kin as the stated recompense for the message
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحْفَظِينَ: those entrusted to preserve the divine trust and sacred knowledge
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةُ: the divinely transmitted bequest or designation of succession
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: his master, guardian, or authority-holder in the declaration concerning Ali عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith connect Ghadir, Ahl al-Bayt, and the inheritance of prophetic knowledge to Imam Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the continuity of divine وصيّة and sacred knowledge from earlier Prophets to the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله and then to Imam Ali عليه السلام. It links this succession to Quranic passages on أهل البيت, أُولِي الْأَمْرِ, المودّة في القربى, and the declaration at Ghadir, presenting Imam Ali عليه السلام as the divinely designated bearer of inherited prophetic knowledge and authority.
